title: Expectancy: does your strategy pay?
desc: Mix win rate, average win and average loss into one number

cards.title: Does it pay?
cards.situation: Your journal shows you win 40% of trades. Your average win is $300. Your average loss is $100. Does your strategy pay?

options.text: No: you lose most of your trades
options.feedback: Losing most trades is fine when the wins are much bigger than the losses.

options.text: Yes: about +$60 a trade on average
options.feedback: Your wins are big enough to cover your losses and more.

options.text: Can’t tell until you win more often
options.feedback: You can tell now: 120 trades is a fair sample. Weight each result by how often it happens.

cards.title: Expectancy
cards.text: [[expectancy|Expectancy]] is what a strategy makes **per trade, on average**, over many trades. It mixes [[win-rate|how often you win]] with how big the wins and losses are.

visual.foot: Above zero: it pays over many trades. Below zero: it loses.

blocks.tip: It’s an average over many trades. It says nothing sure about the next one.

cards.title: High win rate, losing strategy
cards.text: Strategy A wins most of the time. Strategy B loses most of the time. Which one pays?

visual.label: A: 70% wins, $50 average win, $150 average loss, −$10. B: 40%, $200, $100, +$20

cards.foot: A high win rate can hide a losing strategy.

cards.title: Small samples lie
cards.text: Ten trades prove almost nothing. A lucky run can make a bad strategy look great. Take fees off every trade, wins and losses.

visual.label: 10 trades: luck. 30 trades: a first hint. 100+ trades: worth trusting

cards.rule: track every trade in a journal before you trust the numbers.

cards.title: Work out the expectancy
cards.q: You win 50% of trades. Average win $150, average loss $100. What’s your expectancy per trade?

options.feedback: $150 − $100 ignores how often each one happens. Weight each by its rate.
Half the time you make $150, half the time you lose $100: $75 − $50 a trade.
The sign flipped. Your wins are bigger than your losses at the same rate, so it’s above zero.
That’s only the winning half. Take off the losing half: 0.5 × $100.

cards.title: Reading the number
cards.q: Your strategy’s expectancy is +$20 a trade. What does that mean?

options.text: You’ll make $20 on your next trade
options.feedback: The next trade can still lose. Expectancy is an average that shows up over many trades.

options.text: Over many trades, you average about +$20 each
options.feedback: Some trades win, some lose. Over many of them, they average out near +$20.
That’s a win rate. Expectancy is dollars per trade, on average.
You can still lose, on a trade or a bad run. It only pays on average, over many trades.

cards.headline: You can tell if a strategy pays.
lines: Expectancy = (win rate × avg win) − (loss rate × avg loss).
Above zero pays over many trades.
Trust it only after a big sample of trades.
